newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles higher on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles higher on shortcovering.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Monday, rebounding from recent losses due to shortcovering.
"It's a little shortcovering, but the market is just muddling," said an East Coast paper broker.
The electricity complex trended lower last week on growing concerns over ample hydroelectric supplies in the western U.S. through the first half of 1997.
"The perception was that it was oversold," said a New York futures broker.

March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up 48 cents at $10.88 a megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a session low of $10.50. April COB finished up 35 cents at $10.05. Other COB months ended 15 to 30 cents higher.
March Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 43 cents at $13.13 after bouncing between $12.70 and $13.25. April PV finished up 30 cents at $12.10. Other active PV contracts ended 10 to 20 cents higher.
While front-month power contracts appeared weak despite today's bounce, the back-months seemed supported by strength of their corresponding natural gas futures contracts, market sources said.
"The summer months (in gas futures) look rather well bid from April on. That could carry over to electricity," said the futures broker.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 7.2 cents at $2.313 per milion British thermal units. The April contract finished down 3.2 cents at $2.107.
Swing gas deliveries at the San Juan Hub in New Mexico were traded near $2.30/mmBtu.
This week, the Pacific Northwest was forcast to experience above normal temperatures in 40-50 degrees F during day and 20s-30s at night, with variable clouds across the region.

In the meantime, the Southwest would receive above normal temperatures with normal precipitation across California and Nevada. Day readings would average in the 60s-70s and night readings would range in the 30s-40s.
A 1,100 megawatt (MW) pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut Saturday to repair a mechanical problem, and could stay shut up to two weeks.
The 790 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant near Laughlin, Nev., was expected to restart early Tuesday after being shut Friday due to a tube leak.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant at Richland, Wash., was running at 58 percent power for ongoing work on its recirculation pumps.
NYMEX estimated 246 COB and 105 PV contracts were sold, down from Friday's sales of 385 COB and 208 PV.
